Source conflict. We show SRM’s 2026-27 rule (for the 2026-27 cycle; SRM may revise for 2027 entry): at least 60% aggregate in Physics, Mathematics and one more qualifying subject. Biotechnology and biomedical programmes need 60% in PCM, PMB, PCB or similar combinations. In 75 of the 106 offerings in SRM’s fee table, older text still says 50% and cites SRMJEEE (UG) 2022.

See both versions
2026–2027 Rule Breakdown (for the 2026-27 cycle; SRM may revise for 2027 entry)
Qualifying Examination: Applicant should have passed in Higher Secondary examination (10+2 pattern) or appearing in Higher Secondary examination in the current academic year with a minimum of 60% aggregate (3 subjects) in Physics (mandatory), Mathematics (mandatory) and at least one of Chemistry / Biotechnology / Biology / Computer Science / Information Technology / Informatics Practices / Engineering Graphics / Botany and Zoology.
Biotechnology & Biomedical: Minimum 60% aggregate in PCM / PMB / PCB / PCB or Z (Botany or Zoology). Students who have not studied Mathematics in 10+2 must undertake an additional 4-credit course in Mathematics during the first year.
Residency and age: Resident Indian. Should have attained the age of 16 years and 6 months on the 31st July of the calendar year in which the 12th Board examination is held.
Entrance Exam: Admission is through the national-level entrance exam SRMJEEE (UG).
